outcome: CAP-03.S03 now exposes every accepted-bound large-lineage limit as explicit incomplete authority across the SQLite repository, authenticated Core response, OpenAPI and generated client, and Audit and Lineage workspace. Cursor and scan truncation force integrity-review, deny export, and remain visible to the researcher. The repository uses stable breadth-first traversal in bounded 256-revision snapshot batches and materializes no more than the requested page of LineageNode projections. A real 4,161-revision, 16,642-fact Windows SQLite fixture proves the cursor and scan boundaries, restart-stable ordering, bounded page materialization, fail-closed export, and a 7.163-second p95 against an 18-second regression limit.

rootCauseAnalysis.rootCause: The original repository treated its internal cursor and scan ceilings as invisible implementation details. When a true continuation crossed the cursor ceiling, it returned a terminal null cursor without changing integrity or export authority. When the breadth-first frontier crossed the scan ceiling, it stopped silently. The renderer correctly treated a null cursor as complete because the cross-process contract carried no truncation fact. The same implementation rebuilt and materialized the complete bounded graph for every page with per-revision and per-event queries, and the slice evidence had no representative cardinality benchmark to expose either behavior.
rootCauseAnalysis.correction: The LineagePage contract now carries a strict truncated/truncationReason pair. Both limits force integrity-review and integrity-review export denial in the repository and Pydantic response model; the generator, exact generated decoder/client, pagination merge, readiness predicate, and UI preserve that authority monotonically. Traversal is breadth-first but batches at most 256 revisions per indexed SQLite snapshot and materializes at most pageSize LineageNode objects. A governed benchmark creates and reopens a real project above the 10,100-fact boundary and separately exercises the scan limit.
rootCauseAnalysis.whyPriorTestsMissedIt: Prior unit, integration, client, and renderer fixtures all remained below both internal ceilings. They proved ordinary pagination and downstream monotonicity but never modeled a true has-more state beyond 10,000 or an unvisited frontier at the scan budget. Section 11 required a representative benchmark, but R01 did not include one.
rootCauseAnalysis.prevention: The new fields are part of OpenAPI and generated TypeScript, server and client semantic validators reject contradictory authority, SQLite/Core/client/renderer tests exercise both limit reasons and denial behavior, the large-lineage performance tool is included in governed Ruff/mypy scope, and this slice evidence records an explicit performance threshold and raw samples.
